[2026-05-22 22:55] Quick read-only check — credentials.env probe.

PO is trying to recover the existing `mvox-dev` Cloudflare API token (already issued per CF dashboard, status Active, scope `Account: Cloudflare Pages: Edit`). The dashboard only shows token values at creation — can't view it later. Hoping it was stashed in your credentials file.

### What to do

Inspect `~/.config/mvox/credentials.env` for a `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` entry. Report **presence/absence + key-name + length** only — DO NOT echo the value. Same discipline as the ENTU_API_KEY handling.

Example output shape (one line, value-masked):
```
CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: present (length=40)
```
or
```
CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: absent
Other CF-related keys in file: CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID (present), CLOUDFLARE_ZONE_ID (absent)
```

If absent, list any OTHER credentials in the file (names only, no values) — PO may have used a different env-var name.

Suggested command:
```bash
grep -E '^[A-Z_]+=' ~/.config/mvox/credentials.env 2>/dev/null | awk -F= '{ printf "%s: present (length=%d)\n", $1, length($2) }'
```
That outputs key names + lengths without exposing values.

### When done
SendMessage with the probe result. No further action needed from you — PO will use the info to either export the recovered value or roll a fresh token.

### Tool-restriction reminder
Single quick read. If anything is unexpected (file missing, permission denied, malformed entries) — report instead of guessing.
summary: Quick check: is CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN in credentials.env?
